title: The post-fall review in five checks
objectives: Run the five post-fall checks and say what each action could be.
Explain why a fall lowers the equity share — and what rebalancing then means.
body_md:
1. Fund vs benchmark: fund return vs its TRI over the same period. If in line, it's the market, not the fund: no change. 2. Fund vs category: rank and rolling returns over 3–5 years. Replace only on sustained under-performance, not one bad year. 3. Goal date: years left until the money is needed. If near, follow the glide path to debt; if far, stay the course. 4. Asset mix: equity share now vs target. A fall lowers the equity share; rebalancing may mean adding to equity. 5. Client's comfort: how the client felt and acted. If the fall caused real distress, revisit the risk profile calmly, not mid-panic.

| Check | What to look at | Possible action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Fund vs benchmark | Fund return vs its TRI over the same period | If in line, it's the market, not the fund: no change |
| 2. Fund vs category | Rank and rolling returns over 3–5 years | Replace only on sustained under-performance, not one bad year |
| 3. Goal date | Years left until the money is needed | If near, follow the glide path to debt; if far, stay the course |
| 4. Asset mix | Equity share now vs target | A fall lowers the equity share; rebalancing may mean adding to equity |
| 5. Client's comfort | How the client felt and acted | If the fall caused real distress, revisit the risk profile calmly, not mid-panic |

> **Investor takeaway:** Review after a fall with the same calm checks as any other time: benchmark, category, goal date, mix.
example: Fund −18%, benchmark −20%: in line — it's the market, not the fund; no change. Fund −10%, benchmark +5%: a fund problem to review.
say: If in line with the benchmark, it's the market, not the fund.
Replace only on sustained under-performance, not one bad year.
never: Switch funds just because they fell with the market.

check.q: A target 60:40 equity:debt mix drifts to 50:50 after a fall. Rebalancing means…
o: Moving money from debt into equity
check.why: Moving money from debt into equity. Rebalancing back to 60:40 buys equity after prices have fallen.

check.q: A 60:40 mix drifted to 50:50 after a fall. Rebalancing back means:
o: Moving money from debt into equity
check.why: Restoring the target mix moves money from debt into equity after a fall.

check.q: In the post-fall review, fund vs category is judged over:
o: 3–5 years of rank and rolling returns
check.why: Fund vs category: rank and rolling returns over 3–5 years. Replace only on sustained under-performance, not one bad year.
